# LegatorOCR 0.2.0-pre.63

- **Folded pages, half of the text without OCR:** the pass that reads again the ink Tesseract left out dropped any block taller than a line (a whole paragraph or half a page, exactly what a fold produces). Such a block is now read as a whole (`--psm 6`), cut into lines, and its words are kept only if they are clean and do not lie on words already there. Blocks taller than 70 % of the page (pictures, dark panels) are left alone; at most 4 blocks per page.
- **Margin 2–40 mm** with a typed value next to the slider (before: slider 0–30 mm).
- **Less waiting when turning pages:** once the page on screen is done and the settings have been still for 0.7 s, the next and the previous page are processed in the background (one at a time, never ahead of the page being looked at); up to 5 previews are kept in memory.

Known: the block rescue was tested on a synthetic block and on the unit level, not on the real folded pages (the photos were not available here). The processing itself was not made faster and does not use the graphics card: on a 4096×3072 synthetic photo it took 1.2 s without OCR and 4.7 s with OCR and perspective; the read-ahead hides the wait, it does not shorten it. GPU processing would be a separate, large piece of work.
